subject.title: Feature: Private Mode for demos and content creation

question: What exact privacy guarantee and activation authority should OpenClaw support for private sessions across core and plugin-owned persistence surfaces?
rationale: The implementation cannot safely proceed until maintainers define whether the feature means only no transcript and workspace context, or a broader zero-durable-trace promise covering memory, tools, media, logs, plugins, metrics, backups, and channel policy.

options.title: Bounded private sessions
options.body: Guarantee no workspace or memory injection and no durable transcript/session content, while explicitly documenting allowed operational metadata and plugin limitations.

options.title: Zero durable trace
options.body: Require all core and plugin persistence, logs, media, indexing, metrics, and recovery artifacts to remain memory-only or be rejected, accepting substantially larger architecture and compatibility work.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Keep existing context-injection controls and deletion/pruning tools without presenting a new security guarantee until the full boundary can be enforced.

recommendation.title: Bounded private sessions
recommendation.body: Guarantee no workspace or memory injection and no durable transcript/session content, while explicitly documenting allowed operational metadata and plugin limitations.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available routing signal is the recent canonical-session review plus repeated history across the central protocol, session-server, and persisted-state files.
